name: PUEO
summary: The successor to ANITA uses interferometric triggering to search for faint radio signatures of ultra-high-energy neutrinos from a stratospheric balloon over Antarctica.
detection_principle: A large dual-polarisation antenna payload detects Askaryan pulses from ice and radio pulses from tau-induced air showers. Real-time beamforming lowers the trigger threshold compared with earlier balloon instruments.

sites.name: Antarctica; high-altitude balloon flights observing Antarctic ice
sites.location: Antarctica; high-altitude balloon flights observing Antarctic ice

status.label: Multiple stages
status.evidence: First flight completed in January 2026; the recovered dataset is in analysis.

timeline.event: Payload landed after a successful flight; data recovered.

key_parameters.name: 2020 white-paper instrument design
key_parameters.value: 108 dual-polarisation horn antennas with beamforming trigger; the flight configuration evolved during development

results.summary: The university reports a completed flight and recovered data. A completed flight is not a published neutrino detection.
